title: Luck is in Numbers
statementMd:
Vasya has been collecting transport tickets for quite a while now. His collection contains several thousands of tram, trolleybus and bus tickets. Vasya is already fed up with the traditional definition of what a lucky ticket is. Thus, he's looking for new perspectives on that. Besides, Vasya cannot understand why all tickets are only divided into lucky and unlucky ones. He thinks that all tickets are lucky but in different degrees. Having given the matter some thought, Vasya worked out the definition of a ticket's *degree of luckiness*. Let a ticket consist of $2*n*$ digits. Let's regard each digit as written as is shown on the picture:

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/35a3f1412c4be65fa4a443fb9da7cc28025135c6.png)

You have seen such digits on electronic clocks: seven segments are used to show digits. Each segment can either be colored or not. The colored segments form a digit. Vasya regards the digits as written in this very way and takes the right half of the ticket and puts it one the left one, so that the first digit coincides with the $*n* + 1$-th one, the second digit coincides with the $*n* + 2$-th one, ..., the $*n*$-th digit coincides with the $2*n*$-th one. For each pair of digits, put one on another, he counts the number of segments colored in both digits and summarizes the resulting numbers. The resulting value is called the *degree of luckiness* of a ticket. For example, the degree of luckiness of ticket 03 equals four and the degree of luckiness of ticket 2345 equals six.

You are given the number of a ticket containing $2*n*$ digits. Your task is to find among the tickets whose number exceeds the number of this ticket but also consists of $2*n*$ digits such ticket, whose degree of luckiness exceeds the degrees of luckiness of the given ticket. Moreover, if there are several such tickets, you should only choose the one with the smallest number.

## Input

The first line contains the number of the ticket that consists of $*k*$ characters ($*k* = 2*n*, 1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$).

## Output

Print the number of the sought ticket or "-1" (without the quotes) if no such ticket exists.
statementZhMd:
瓦夏收集车票已经有相当长一段时间了。他的收藏中有数千张电车、无轨电车和公交车票。瓦夏已经厌倦了关于幸运车票的传统定义。因此，他正在寻找新的思路。此外，瓦夏无法理解为什么所有车票只能被分为幸运和不幸运两类。他认为所有车票都是幸运的，只是幸运程度不同。经过一番思考，瓦夏提出了车票的*幸运度*定义。设一张车票由 $2*n*$ 位数字组成。我们按照下图所示的方式书写每一位数字：

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/35a3f1412c4be65fa4a443fb9da7cc28025135c6.png)

你一定在电子钟上见过这样的数字：使用七段数码管来显示数字。每一段都可以被点亮或不被点亮，被点亮的数码管组成一个数字。瓦夏认为数字就是以这种方式书写的。他将车票的右半部分放到左半部分上，使第一位数字与第 $*n* + 1$ 位重合，第二位数字与第 $*n* + 2$ 位重合，……，第 $*n*$ 位数字与第 $2*n*$ 位重合。对于每一对相互重叠的数字，他计算两个数字中同时被点亮的数码管数量，并将这些数量相加。所得的值称为车票的*幸运度*。例如，车票 03 的幸运度为 4，车票 2345 的幸运度为 6。

给定一张包含 $2*n*$ 位数字的车票号码。你的任务是在所有号码大于给定车票号码且同样由 $2*n*$ 位数字组成的车票中，寻找一张幸运度大于给定车票幸运度的车票。此外，如果有多张符合条件的车票，你应当选择号码最小的那一张。

## 输入格式

第一行包含车票号码，该号码由 $*k*$ 个字符组成（$*k* = 2*n*, 1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$）。

## 输出格式

输出所求车票的号码。如果不存在这样的车票，则输出 "-1"（不含引号）。
